lots.guide_summary: A$502 to A$933 from 7 close SOLD results at Theriault's (US specialist doll auctions, 2006 to 2024, converted at USD 1 = AUD 1.4359, mostly excellent-condition dolls in collector sales). Category-guide sold results run from A$359 to A$2,441. No UNSOLD comparables. Three snippet-only ASKING leads (A$343 to A$754, category guide only, unverified) are not in the range. No Tasmanian or Australian sale of a comparable doll was found; the newest close sale (29/09/2024) is just over 24 months old.
lots.working: No SOLD same-item sale within the last 24 months (cut-off 19/10/2024): the most recent close result, Theriault's lot 354 at US$450 on 29/09/2024, is about 3 weeks outside the window, and the rest are 2006 to 2022. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0 under the rules. For information only: if the 2024 result counted, keep would be A$646.15 / 1.22 = A$529.63, rounded down A$525; but that is a US specialist room price for an excellent doll, and Tasmanian rooms (Gowans) show no comparable antique Parian ladies at all, so even that figure would be optimistic for a doll with an unchecked head and ruined dress.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark read (back of shoulder plate not shown), condition of head not checked for hairlines, possibility of a reproduction, and no SOLD evidence inside 24 months. Theriault's prices verified on pages opened, but they are US collector-sale results.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: (1) Gowans lot 387386, two Armand Marseille open-mouth child dolls, A$115: verified sale_price 11500 but a different type (20th-century child dolls on composition bodies), not the same item. (2) Gowans lot 400335, vintage German child doll, A$14: verified 1400 but not comparable, same reason. (3) eBay.ca 'Parian-Doll' category page at C$320.24: the URL is a category page, not the item, eBay is closed to us, and the snippet cannot be checked, so it is not even usable as a lead. Kept but marked as unverified leads only: the two Ruby Lane and one Etsy asking prices (snippet only). All 15 Theriault's prices and dates were re-opened and confirmed (sold_price fields match). Minor correction: Theriault's lot 649 event is dated 19/05/2006 on the page, not 20/05/2006.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged head crop: untinted matte bisque with heavy cheek blush, bright cobalt painted eyes with red upper lid line, single-stroke brows, closed orange-red mouth, pierced ear with metal hook and white glass or pearl drop. Hair is pale blonde, comb-marked, with a moulded bow and band at the crown with gilt touches. No visible chips or hairlines at photo resolution, but the shoulder plate is under the dress and the back is not shown. Cloth chest is visible through the torn bodice and is pink-stained. Lower legs bisque with black glossy painted boots, both appear intact. Arms hidden by sleeves. Dress is mauve silk, shredded with large losses at the skirt, with synthetic-looking lace trim (possibly a later redressing).
lots.condition: Head appears clean and undamaged in photos but not checked for hairlines or repairs; shoulder plate and back unseen. Costume shredded with missing sections; cloth body stained. Legs and boots appear intact. Arms not visible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Could you check the back of the shoulder plate for any incised mark, number, artist signature or date (reproductions are often signed and dated), look for hairline cracks or repairs to the head and shoulder plate under good light, tell us whether the lower arms are bisque, leather or cloth and whether both hands are intact, and confirm the height?

lots.working: Keep: lowest same-maker vase SOLD within 24 months = Gowans lot 410177, A$35 hammer (22/05/2026). 35 / 1.22 = 28.69, rounded down to A$25. Flip: likely resale of the pair at a Tasmanian room about A$60 hammer (between the A$35 single vase and A$85 four-piece group); less about 20% seller commission and fees (A$12) and no postage (local room) = A$48; 48 / 2.44 = 19.67, rounded down to A$15. lots.guide_summary: A$50 to A$245. SOLD close: two single Gill 1850s prints at A$50 (Leonard Joel 2025) and A$90 (Davidson 2019), both lithographs from other series. ASKING close: one Sydney dealer's A$85 to A$245 (mostly A$145) for hand-coloured sibling 1857 Gill plates in good condition (4 pages verified, 4 unverified because of rate limiting). No UNSOLD evidence. Category guides: colonial engravings A$90 to A$150 sold; Gill originals A$600 to A$4,000 sold (relevant only if the loose sheet is an original); complete Victoria Illustrated volumes asked at about A$1,000 to A$3,600. All AUD except AbeBooks (USD 1 = AUD 1.4359).
lots.working: No SOLD result for the same plate (or any Victoria Illustrated steel engraving) was found in the last 24 months. The nearest SOLD singles are different Gill prints (A$50 lithograph 2025, A$90 lithograph 2019), so not the same item: keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For information only, a plain colonial steel engraving sold for A$90 (Davidson 2025) and a framed hand-coloured 1863 print for A$130 hammer at Gowans, which suggests the framed Richmond plate is a A$50 to A$130 item at auction, uncoloured and toned.
lots.confidence_reason: Plate inscriptions read clearly in the photos and match the NGV record, but there is no same-item SOLD result, original versus later reprint is unknown, and the loose sheet's nature (print or watercolour) and maker are unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped outright. Re-classed: the Davidson and Leonard Joel Gill originals, Sketch Book and album stay as category guides only. Davidson lot pages no longer show the result to a plain request; the verifier confirmed every Davidson 'Sold for' figure in Davidson's own archive search results instead. lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged plate (photo 3): lower left 'S.T. Gill del.', lower right 'J. Tingle sc.', title 'Approach to Richmond, from North Bank of Yarra Yarra', imprint 'Published by Sands & Kenny, Melbourne & Sydney 1856'. Uncoloured, on toned buff paper with light foxing, vignette image. Frame: period gilt gesso with bead moulding, losses on the top and left edges and corners; glass and back not shown. Loose sheet (photo 2): soft watercolour-like washes over fine pencil or line work, two men (one with spade, one kneeling planting), picket fence, long shed, river with rowing boats; sheet creased, foxed, edges ragged and toned. No signature visible in the photos. Could be a hand-tinted lithograph or an original watercolour; brushwork looks free but resolution is too low to tell.
lots.condition: Engraving toned with light foxing, apparently unstained in the image area; frame has gilt and gesso losses. Loose sheet creased, foxed, edge wear, unframed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the loose coloured sheet a print (look for a plate mark, printed line or dot pattern under a glass) or hand-painted, and is anything signed or inscribed on the front or back? What are its measurements? For the framed Gill engraving, is it glazed, is there any old framer's label or inscription on the back, and is there any staining or tear under the mount?
